c.tagline: Bermuda's pastel harbour capital of Front Street shops and pink-sand beaches.

taxi.fareNote: Bermuda has no Uber or ride-hailing and does not allow visitors to rent cars. Getting around is by metered taxi (fixed government rates), the pink public buses, the Sea Express ferries, or a rented electric minicar or scooter.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across Bermuda.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.St. George's (East End): St. Peter's Church St George's Bermuda

avoid.reason: Use care in the 'back of town' area north of Court Street late at night, where occasional street crime occurs.

hood_desc: Bermuda's compact pastel capital along Front Street, packed with harbourside restaurants, shops, and the island's ferry and bus terminals; the most convenient, walkable base and nightlife hub.
A leafy upscale parish just south of Hamilton fronting Elbow Beach and the eastern South Shore; a relaxed base of resorts and cottage colonies with easy beach access.
The island's southwest, home to Horseshoe Bay and a string of Bermuda's most famous pink-sand beaches plus its biggest resorts; ideal for a beach-focused stay.
A UNESCO World Heritage town at the East End - Bermuda's original 1612 capital, with narrow lanes, St. Peter's Church, and colonial forts; steeped in history.
A green central parish with the Crystal & Fantasy Caves, the Bermuda Aquarium at Flatts Village, and the sheltered Flatts Inlet; quiet and family-friendly.
lodging: Newstead Belmont Hills Golf Resort & Spa

water.note: Rain-collected tap water is generally safe; bottled is widely available if you prefer.

transit.pay: Buses and ferries share zone-based fares; buy paper tickets, tokens, or a multi-day transportation pass at the Hamilton bus and ferry terminals, or pay exact cash on board buses (no change given). A 1-3 day pass covers unlimited bus and ferry travel.
transit.hours: Pink buses run roughly 7am-11pm with reduced Sunday and holiday service; ferries run mainly daytime and early evening and less often in winter. There is little late-night transit, so taxis fill the gap.
transit.note: Visitors cannot rent cars in Bermuda; the pink public buses, the Sea Express ferries across the Great Sound, taxis, and rented electric minicars or scooters are how everyone gets around.

bus: Bermuda Public Transportation Board (island-wide pink bus network)
ferry: Sea Express ferries (Hamilton, Paget/Warwick, Dockyard, and seasonal St. George's routes)

car.idp: Not applicable - visitors may not rent cars; electric minicars and scooters are the rental option

transit.m: Taxi to City of Hamilton (20-30 min)
Public bus Route 1, 3, 10 or 11 to Hamilton (45-60 min)

tip.r: A 15-17% service charge (the 'gratuity') is typically added to hotel and restaurant bills; otherwise 15-20% is standard for taxis and dining.

landmarks: Front Street
Pastel colonial buildings with shaded verandas line Hamilton Harbour's main promenade, Bermuda's premier strip for shopping, dining and watching cruise ships glide past.
Cathedral of the Most Holy Trinity (Bermuda Cathedral)
Climb the 155-step tower of this neo-Gothic limestone cathedral for the finest 360-degree panorama over Hamilton's rooftops and turquoise harbour.
Fort Hamilton
A Victorian polygonal fortress ringed by a moat garden of giant ferns, its ramparts and underground galleries overlook the city and harbour for free.
Bermuda Underwater Exploration Institute (BUEI)
Dive Bermuda's famous shipwrecks and abyssal depths through immersive exhibits, treasure collections and a simulated 3,700-meter submersible plunge on Hamilton's waterfront.
City Hall and Arts Centre
Topped by a bronze weathervane of the Sea Venture, this elegant 1960 landmark houses the Bermuda National Gallery and Society of Arts exhibitions.
Sessions House
Bermuda's Italianate parliament building of 1819, with its Jubilee clock tower, hosts the world's oldest continuous parliament outside Britain—wig-wearing sessions included.
Queen Elizabeth Park (Par-la-Ville Gardens)
Hamilton's beloved pocket park blooms behind the historic Perot Post Office, offering shaded benches, sculpture and the famous moongate for lunchtime lingering.
Perot Post Office and Bermuda Historical Society Museum
The charming 1840s post office where Bermuda's first stamps were struck adjoins a small museum of cedar furniture, maps and colonial curiosities.
Albuoy's Point and the Birdcage
This waterfront park beside the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club offers harbour views, while the nearby 'Birdcage' traffic box remains Hamilton's quirkiest photo stop.
Victoria Park
A gingerbread Victorian bandstand from 1889 crowns this sunken garden north of downtown, a leafy concert venue commemorating Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee.

train.note: Bermuda has no railway; the former Bermuda Railway line is now the Railway Trail walking and cycling path.

bus.note: Bermuda's pink public buses run island-wide from the central terminal in the City of Hamilton to every parish, from St. George's in the East End to the Royal Naval Dockyard in the West End; there are no international bus routes (Bermuda is a remote mid-Atlantic island).

ferry.note: Sea Express ferries cross Hamilton Harbour and the Great Sound, linking the City of Hamilton with Paget, Warwick, the Royal Naval Dockyard, and (seasonally) St. George's; there are no international ferry connections.

half.name: Royal Naval Dockyard
half.blurb: Restored 19th-century naval fortress at the West End with the National Museum of Bermuda, dolphin encounters, and a craft market.

half.name: Crystal & Fantasy Caves
half.blurb: Illuminated limestone caverns with crystal-clear underground pools in Hamilton Parish.

half.name: Horseshoe Bay Beach
half.blurb: Bermuda's most famous pink-sand beach on the South Shore, with coves and snorkeling.

full.name: St. George's
full.blurb: UNESCO-listed 17th-century town with St. Peter's Church, colonial forts, and Tobacco Bay snorkeling.

full.name: Bermuda Railway Trail
full.blurb: Traffic-free coastal walking and cycling path following the old railway line across the island.
